input.command:
cat > README.md <<'MD'
# Order of Play

A to-do list that keeps itself the way a tournament keeps its order of play: matches on the board,
courts assigned, a rubber stamp on anything that finishes. Express on the back, no framework on the front.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm start          # http://localhost:3000
npm run dev        # same, with node --watch
npm test           # 16 tests, node:test
```

Environment:

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | `3000` | Port to listen on |
| `TODO_DATA_FILE` | `data/todos.json` | Where the schedule is stored (relative to the project root) |

## API

| Method | Route | Body | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/todos` | | `{ todos, summary: { total, done, remaining } }` |
| `POST` | `/api/todos` | `{ title, note?, court? }` | `201 { todo }` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/todos/:id` | any of `{ title, note, court, done }` | `200 { todo }` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/todos/completed` | | `200 { removed }` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/todos/:id` | | `204` |

`title` is required, trimmed, and capped at 200 characters. `note` is capped at 500. `court` must be a
whole number from 1 to 18 or `null`. Bad input comes back `400 { error }`, an unknown id `404 { error }`.

Ticking a todo stamps `completedAt`; un-ticking it clears the stamp again.

## How it is put together

```
server.js        boots the store, wires the port, handles SIGINT/SIGTERM
src/app.js       the Express app: JSON routes, static files, error handler
src/store.js     the data layer
public/          the programme: index.html, styles.css, app.js
test/api.test.js the suite, driven over real HTTP on an ephemeral port
```

`src/app.js` exports `createApp(store)` rather than listening itself, so the tests build an app around a
throwaway store in a temp directory and never touch your real schedule.

`src/store.js` holds the list in memory and writes the whole file on every mutation. Two details matter:
mutations run through a promise queue so concurrent requests cannot interleave a read-modify-write, and
each write lands in a temp file that is then `rename()`d over the target, so a crash mid-write leaves the
previous file intact. A mutation that throws validation rolls the in-memory list back to its snapshot, so
a rejected request never leaves a half-applied change behind.

## The front end

No build step, no framework. `public/app.js` is a module that talks to the same JSON API and renders rows
with `createElement` and `textContent`, so a todo titled `<script>` is just text.

The look is a printed matchday programme: Bodoni Moda for display, IBM Plex Sans for text, IBM Plex Mono
for the numerals, hairline rules, and a single ochre accent. Dark mode is the night session under the
floodlights. Keyboard: `Enter` schedules, double-click or `Rename` edits a title in place, `Enter` saves,
`Escape` cancels.
MD
echo "--- README written ---"

content.text:
Game, set, match. Here's the scorecard.

## What you've got

**`new-entire-demo/`** is a working Express to-do app called **Order of Play**, on a new branch `todo-express` cut from `origin/main`.

```
server.js          boots the store, binds the port, handles SIGINT/SIGTERM
src/app.js         createApp(store): JSON routes, static files, error handler
src/store.js       file-backed data layer
public/            index.html, styles.css, app.js (no build step)
test/api.test.js   16 tests over real HTTP
```

**API:** `GET /api/todos`, `POST /api/todos`, `PATCH /api/todos/:id`, `DELETE /api/todos/completed`, `DELETE /api/todos/:id`. Validation returns `400 {error}`, unknown ids `404`.

Two things in `src/store.js` that a quick version usually skips: mutations run through a promise queue so two concurrent requests cannot interleave a read-modify-write, and every write goes to a temp file then `rename()`s over the target, so a crash mid-write leaves the old file intact. A failed validation rolls the in-memory list back to its snapshot. `app.js` exports `createApp(store)` instead of listening itself, so tests build an app around a throwaway store in a temp dir.

**The look:** a printed matchday programme, not a framework default. Bodoni Moda against IBM Plex Sans and Plex Mono, hairline rules, one ochre accent, zero border-radius, and a rotated `COMPLETED` rubber stamp in the margin of finished rows. Dark mode is the night session under floodlights.

## Verification actually run

- `npm test`: **16/16 passing**, including persistence across a restart and 25 concurrent writes landing intact on disk.
- Live server smoke test on a real port: create, toggle, list, static assets all `200`, empty title `400`.
- Rendered it in headless Chromium at 1280px and 420px, plus a CDP-emulated dark-mode capture. That caught two real faults I then fixed: the paper sheen was washing the dark background grey, and the eyebrow text fell below readable contrast on dark. Both corrected and re-verified.

## Needs your call

Nothing is committed. The work sits untracked at `new-entire-demo/` on branch `todo-express`. Say the word and I'll commit.

One honest flag on tracking: `entire status` still records this session's branch as `main`, since that is where it started before I cut the task branch. The session is enabled and active and will capture on commit, but that branch field is stale metadata rather than a live read.

To take it for a hit:

```bash
cd new-entire-demo && npm start   # http://localhost:3000
```

As Ted would put it, it's not about being the best list in the room, it's about being a list that helps you get better. Be curious, not judgmental, about what you put on it.
commit and push
Authorized. Recheck first, then commit and push.
